doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: Offers to leave New Orleans and his brother's playing
summary: Bailey turned down offers from bands elsewhere and says nobody taught him; Allen asks about his brother's age.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: bands. As I said, I played in some first class bands.

And I went away from here, I could have played in the Butterstock Band from Nashville, Mississippi, he used to play on Steamer Capital. He wanted me. I wanted to build up a home over there. And then Turt Johnson, the band, I don't know if he's from Baton Rouge, he wanted to fire his drum and take me. I was playing Jack Carey, I was playing Jack Carey, and my brother was playing bass, plays Brown. Then another place called, let me see, I believe it was Port Island, went to play. And there was a band up there that's called the Stores Band. They wanted me to play with them. I didn't want to leave town, they wanted me to stay up there, I didn't want to stay. I'm born and raised in New Orleans, I don't know how to play with New Orleans. I could have been to New York, I could have been to Chicago, I didn't want to leave. I could have been just like Lewis, my younger days. Brother Damon was up there, I said no. I said I don't want to make this stuff. So I went up there, I was a bit of a hump as a cat. I could have went up there and Lewis played with us. When he first came out of Jones, my brother was the first one to grab him. He had a little old brass on, all bent. He couldn't play with four or five numbers. My brother got in and broke him in. I had a brother broke with me, we should play with every side of the night over the river. The brick building, on the broken corner, every side of the night. And then we got broke in and got him a new home, made up a band. Went down to the winter count on the winter guard down there, Joe Oliver. Joe Oliver took him, he gave me food out there, Joe Oliver was all the last time I was just going there. But nobody learned me how to play. It's just a gift of all.
But what is the difference between your brother's age and yours?
I couldn't tell you on that.
Is he much younger than you or older?
I couldn't say it. Because see I left my people, I lost my people. Howdy, how you doing?
